rows.en:
Hello.
My name is Reiko Fukuzawa.
I'm just a first-year, same as {c}{f:|}.
Nice to meet you, everyone.
Umm, the scary story I'm going to tell is about the old school building.
It's a pretty famous story, so you might all know it already.
It's about the stairs in the old school building.
{c}{f:|}, have you heard the story of the thirteen steps?
Even with stairs, you know, some numbers of steps are creepy.
People always say thirteen is an unlucky number in the West, right?
Even you know Friday the thirteenth is bad luck, right, {c}{f:|}?
Well, stairs with thirteen steps are bad news too.{p}

Do you know why?
Thirteen steps are the stairs up to the gallows.
One kind of death penalty is hanging, right?
Hanging. Hanging by the neck.
The stairs you climb to get up on the gallows have exactly thirteen steps.
So when people say thirteen steps, they mean the stairs up to the gallows.
And that's why people normally don't build stairs with thirteen steps, apparently.
{c}{f:|}, is your house two stories?
Have you ever counted the steps on the stairs at home?
Maybe yours have thirteen steps.
They say thirteen steps will put a curse on you, so you'd better be carefuuul.{p}

Ahahahaha...
Anyway, about the old school building.{p}

Of course, the old school building doesn't have any stairs with thirteen steps either.
They all have fourteen steps.
...But, you know, on Friday the thirteenth, at the far right end of the old school building... the south side, was it?
If you count the stairs there, the ones that should have fourteen steps only have thirteen, apparently.
And if you try to check whether it's true, something bad happens to you, they say.{p}Had you heard that rumor?
I'd heard it
I hadn't heard it

Oh, so you'd heard it.
Well, it is a famous story.
There are all kinds of versions of the story about those stairs.
Like, you count fourteen steps going up, but when you count them going down, there are thirteen.
But, you know, don't you sometimes mess up when you count stairs?
Do you count the very top step, or are you not supposed to count it?
Haven't you ever been unsure?
Well, that one's not actually a step, see.
It's the floor.
So you don't include it in the count.
So when you count steps, you only count the part sandwiched between one floor and the next.{p}

Did you learn something?
Ahahahaha...
Or did you know that much already?
...Sorry, sorry.
So, the story of the old school building's thirteen steps.
{c}{f:|}, if you knew the rumor, didn't you want to try it out?{p}You did, didn't you?
I wanted to
I didn't want to
Oh, so you did want to.{p}So, did you actually try it?
I tried it
I didn't try it
There hasn't been a Friday the 13th since I started at this school

Oh, that's right.
You're right about that.
There hasn't been a single Friday the thirteenth since we started at this school.
...Eheheheh.
But you know, there's a way to check even when it isn't Friday the thirteenth.{p}

I know how.
You know those tear-off calendars?
You set one to Friday the thirteenth.
Then you hang it on the wall by the thirteen steps from the rumor.
If you do that, the same thing happens, they say.
Bet you didn't know that.
But I guess it's still weaker that way.
They say that unless you've got a really strong sixth sense, the stairs won't turn into thirteen steps.
But if they do turn into thirteen, that's awful too, right?
"Yaaay!
It's thirteen steps!"
Even if you say that, in the end nothing but bad things happen, right?
But still, you're curious, aren't you?
Don't rumors like that just make you really want to try them?
And you said you wanted to try it too, {c}{f:|}.
So, well, I went and tried it.{p}

Not by myself, of course.
There were three of us.
No way I'd go alone.
It'd be way too scary.
Girls from my class.{p}

A girl named Sanae Motoki, and Yoko Someya.
They're both weird girls.
They're not exactly normal, you know?
Well, Yoko isn't as weird as Sanae.
Honestly, Sanae is a seriously weird girl.
...Oh, that has nothing to do with this, does it?
I'll tell you just how weird Sanae is some other time.
Actually, it was Sanae who told me about the tear-off calendar thing, too.
She's got a special informant, you see.{p}

So the three of us went.
To the old school building, to check it out.
When was that, again?
I think it was the thirteenth of last month... yes, the thirteenth.
It wasn't a Friday, so we brought the tear-off calendar.
We figured that if at least the date was the same, it'd be easier to check.
And if nothing happened, we were planning to go again on a real Friday the thirteenth.
So after school, we snuck into the old school building, which is off-limits.{p}

As a girl bursting with curiosity, I wanted a little taste of adventure, you know?
My heart was really pounding.
It was my first time ever going into the old school building.
The old school building is scary, isn't it?
It's really scary even in broad daylight.
We went there to have a scary experience, right?
So our frame of mind was different.
From the very start we'd convinced ourselves, something scary's going to happen, something scary's going to happen.
So even a perfectly ordinary old school building starts giving you the chills.{p}

The smell of old wood seemed like some kind of nasty, rotten stink.
Even the graffiti carved into the pillars seemed weirdly scary.
It was dead silent, and that alone made it feel like something was there.
Your state of mind at the time really matters, doesn't it?
If we'd gone there to do something really fun, it wouldn't have been scary at all, and the smell of old wood would have felt nostalgic, and the graffiti would have been funny, and we'd have been thinking about other things, I bet.{p}
By the way, {c}{f:|}.{p}Have you ever been to the old school building?
I have
I haven't

Oh, really.
So you have.
How were you feeling when you went there, {c}{f:|}?
Was it fun?{p}Or was it scary?
It was fun
It was scary
I didn't feel anything in particular

Oh, really.
So it was scary.
Not that there was any point in asking.
I just wanted to hear how you felt, {c}{f:|}.
No matter how you answer that question, it's not like the story I'm telling is going to change.{p}

We hung the tear-off calendar firmly on the wall.
"Ow!"
Right then, Yoko caught her hand on a nail.
She cut her finger.
When she squeezed her finger, blood swelled up in a fat little bead on the pad of her index finger.{p}

And Sanae, she went and licked it right off, and said,
"Yummy,"
or something like that.
Funny, right?
Normally she's the kind of girl who bursts into tears at the sight of blood.
The scary mood got blown away, and we all laughed a little.
"Okay, I'll start counting."{p}

Saying that, Yoko started climbing the stairs.
We started climbing with her.{p}

One... two... three...
It makes you pretty nervous, you know.{p}

Normally, you go up stairs without thinking about anything, right?
But there we were, testing our footing with every step, slowly treading our way up the stairs.{p}

And when you go like that, the creak of the wood comes slowly too.
It goes creeeeeeeak, long and dull, and it echoes.{p}

"Ten... eleven... twelve... thirteen.................. fourteen!
It's fourteen!"{p}

The stairs had fourteen steps.
Because our fifteenth step landed on the landing.
"Aww, it's just fourteen."
We looked at each other and laughed.
It was kind of a letdown.
We'd been so scared our hearts were pounding, so it was even more of a disappointment.
"But, you know, we're not at the second floor yet.
This is the halfway point between the first and second floors, so there's still half left."
Saying that, Yoko started up the stairs again.
She was right.
Sanae and I climbed with her.{p}

One... two... three...
We started counting over from the beginning.{p}
Nervously, we counted each step carefully, one by one, so we wouldn't make a mistake.{p}

"Ten... eleven... twelve... thirteen.................. fourteen."
Fourteen steps again.{p}

"It's fourteen after all.
Maybe just hanging up a tear-off calendar like that isn't enough."
"That's not true.
That'll work just fine."
Sanae flatly shot down what I said.{p}

"But we've still got the way down, right?"
Yoko looked happy.
Maybe she wanted to keep that scared feeling going a little longer.
You know how sometimes you just want to see something scary?
That's actually kind of fun, right?
When you're going, so scary, so scary, it's actually pretty fun sometimes.
It was probably that feeling.
That's why Yoko was smiling, I think.
We nodded.{p}

That's right, we still had the way down.
We didn't know how many steps there'd be going down.
So we started counting.
Full of anticipation.{p}
Hey, {c}{f:|}.{p}Do you think we're weird, acting like that?
I think you're weird
You're not weird at all
I was at a loss for words

Hey, that's meaaan!
So that's the kind of person you are, {c}{f:|}.
...You'll pay for this later, just you wait.
Well, for now I'll keep going with the story.
So, we started counting again.{p}

Do you know Bancho Sarayashiki?
Well, whatever, it doesn't matter either way.{p}

"Ah!"
Right as we were counting the steps.
Yoko missed her footing and fell down the stairs.
We were totally shocked.{p}

We forgot all about counting the stairs and rushed over to her.
I mean, Yoko had stopped moving.
We ran over and lifted her up.
She wasn't bleeding, though.
She seemed to have passed out.
"Yoko!
Yoko!"
"..........Mm...nn."
Yoko was alive.
Well, of course, if she'd been dead, that wouldn't have been funny at all.{p}

When Yoko opened her eyes, she started looking all around.
For a moment, it seemed like she didn't know what had happened, or where she was.
I got worried she had amnesia.
But she was okay.
"...I fell down the stairs, didn't I?"
she said, and laughed.
"Come on, let's stop.
The stairs don't have thirteen steps."
That's what I said.
"Yeah.
Let's go."
Yoko agreed with me.{p}

"...What a waste of a tear-off calendar."
Only Sanae looked a little disappointed.{p}

It was like we didn't even exist to her.
"Yoko!"
I called her, but she completely ignored me.
Sanae and I stood at the bottom of the stairs, watching Yoko closely.
Something was wrong with her.{p}

"...It really is thirteen steps.
There are only thirteen steps!
What do I do, Reiko?!"
Saying that, she clung to me, crying.{p}

"It's okay, there's nothing to worry about.
I was counting.
It was fourteen steps, I'm sure of it.
You just miscounted, Yoko!"
I laughed and patted Yoko on the shoulder.
Yoko was trembling.
She was trembling like crazy.{p}

"...Let's get out of here.
It's dangerous to stay here."
Sanae suddenly murmured.
She was in a daze, her eyes kind of unfocused.
Somehow, Sanae scared me even more.
But I was scared too, so I just nodded, uh-huh, uh-huh.
Even then, I was still scared.
So the three of us walked holding hands.{p}

I was in the middle, with Yoko on my left.
And with my right hand, I was holding Sanae's.
Just from holding her hand, I could feel Yoko trembling.
It was so bad I felt like I'd start shaking too.
We were walking side by side when suddenly my left hand got yanked back with a jerk.{p}

"What's wrong?"
I said, and when I looked at Yoko, she was crying.
She'd stopped walking, and her eyes were brimming with tears.
Her whole face was all scrunched up.
"...Reiko.
I can't walk."
That's what Yoko said, crying.{p}

"What are you talking about?
It's okay.
Are you still worried about the stairs?
That stuff's a lie. Come on, let's go."
I said, and pulled on Yoko's hand.
But there was this incredible strength to her, and Yoko wouldn't budge an inch.
And then she said in a shaking voice:{p}

"...No.
I can't move."
"It's okay, really."
I pulled one more time.
But it was no use at all.
Yoko wouldn't move even a little.
"...Reiko.
Will you help me?"
Yoko asked such a weird question.
I told her I'd help her.
Because we're friends.{p}

"...Reiko, there's something on my legs.
That's why I can't walk.
Will you look for me?"
Yoko suddenly said something like that.
"Huh?"
I tilted my head.
I mean, you wouldn't really get what 'something on my legs' means, right?
So I looked at Yoko's legs.{p}

...I couldn't move.
I even forgot to scream. My eyes were glued to Yoko's legs.
Yoko's legs were covered in babies, all clinging to her.
And they were tiny, too.
Those weren't human babies.
They were shaped like humans, but they were only about twenty centimeters long.
They had no hair, and their eyes were weirdly huge.
But puffy eyelids sealed their eyes shut, so it looked like they couldn't see a thing.
A whole bunch of those babies were clinging to Yoko's legs.
Holding on tight, just like they were hugging their mother.
And they were crying in hoarse little voices, waah, waah.
Some of the babies were rubbing their tiny faces against her legs and licking them, lick, lick.
"Yoko, you have to run!"{p}

Sanae grabbed Yoko's arm, said that, and started running.
I ran too, without thinking.
It took both of us just to get her moving.
I never knew I had that much strength in me, though.
At first she resisted when we pulled, but when we both pulled with all our might, she suddenly went light, like a latch had popped loose.
After that, we were desperate to get Yoko out of there.
As we ran, the babies peeled off Yoko's legs and dropped away, one after another.
The babies that fell got flung onto the floor, wailing, waaah, waaah.
Crying even louder than before.
They reached out their hands, trying to cling to Yoko, but we ran faster than they could crawl.
I glanced back, and a chill ran through me.{p}

When we finally made it out of the old school building, we all just pitched forward and fell.
We put our hands on the ground, panting, huff, huff.
It was so hard to breathe.
I'd never been that exhausted before, either.
I was drenched in sweat all over, too.
"...I left the tear-off calendar behind."
Sanae suddenly murmured, sounding disappointed.
"Stop it!
Don't you dare say we're going back."
I was so startled that I raised my voice without meaning to.{p}

When I looked at Yoko's legs, there were no more babies on them.
But Yoko still hadn't stopped trembling.
Her whole body was shaking and shaking.
Well, anyway, that's how we got out of there alive.
But when I took another look at Yoko's legs...{p}

...They were covered in marks like tiny palms, countless ones.
All over her legs, tons of them.
They'd gone bright red, like the marks you get from being slapped.
The marks didn't go away for a while.
She wore long socks to hide them and stuff.
It seemed like she had a pretty hard time.
But ever since then, Yoko's gotten a little strange.{p}

Out of nowhere, she'll cry "waah!" like a baby, or in the middle of class she'll pretend to cradle a baby, going "there, there."
When she does, her eyes are totally gone, and it's scary.
Everyone laughs, thinking it's some weird joke, but Sanae and I are the only ones who know the secret.
It's really not funny, you know?{p}
...That's the end of my story, but a little while ago, {c}{f:|}, you said we were weird, didn't you?{p}

Let's see, inside your bed would be good.
At night, when you get into bed to go to sleep...{p}

There'll be a tiny baby in there.
And it'll cling to your legs.
Hee hee... Earning {f:a girl's|my} grudge is a scary thing, you know.
{c}{f:|}, you must be looking forward to bedtime.
It's going to happen soon, I promise.
...Well then, let's hear the next person's story.
Okay?{p}

Hmm, you don't know it?
There are all kinds of versions of the story about those stairs, and it's pretty famous, too.
Like, when you count them going up there are fourteen steps, but when you count them going down there are thirteen.
But don't you ever mess up when you count stairs?
Do you count the very top step, or are you not supposed to?
Haven't you ever wondered?
Well, that one isn't a step, see.
It's the floor.
So you don't count it as a step.
So the number of steps in a staircase only counts the part sandwiched between one floor and the next.{p}

Learned something?
Ahahahaha...
Or did you already know that much?
...Sorry, sorry.
Anyway, the story of the thirteen steps in the old school building.
There's a way to check it even if it isn't Friday the 13th.{p}

I know how.
You know those tear-off calendars, right?
You set one to Friday the 13th.
And then you hang it on the wall by the thirteen steps from the rumor.
Then they say the same thing happens.
But I guess that way, the effect is weaker after all.
They say unless you've got a really strong sixth sense, the stairs won't turn into thirteen steps.
But if they did, that'd be awful too, right?
"Yay!
It's thirteen steps!"
Even if you said that, in the end nothing but bad things would happen.
But still, it's interesting, isn't it?
Don't rumors like that make you really want to try them?
Hee hee...
I went and tried it.{p}

Hmm...
When I first heard this story, I wanted to try it, though.
But since we started at this school, the 13th has never once fallen on a Friday, right?
So at first I couldn't try it.
Then the other day, I heard something.{p}

You know those tear-off calendars, right?
You set one to Friday the 13th.
And then you hang it on the wall by the thirteen steps from the rumor.
Then they say the same thing happens.
You didn't know that, did you?
But I guess that way, the effect is weaker after all.
They say unless you've got a really strong sixth sense, the stairs won't turn into thirteen steps.
Well, if they did, maybe that'd be awful.
"Yay!
It's thirteen steps!"
Even if you said that, in the end nothing but bad things would happen.
But still, it's interesting, isn't it?
Don't rumors like that make you really want to try them?
So, you know, I went and tried it.{p}

No way!
Since we started school here, there hasn't been a single Friday the 13th, right?
Or wait, did you know about that method?
The way to check the mystery of the thirteen steps even when it isn't Friday the 13th...
Right, right, you set a tear-off calendar to Friday the 13th.
The one where you just hang it on the wall by the thirteen steps and you're set.
Oh, so you knew about it, huh?
So how did it go?
Did something happen?
...Looks like nothing happened.
That's what your face is saying.
But you know, I hear the tear-off calendar method is weak.
They say unless you've got serious spiritual power, the stairs won't turn into thirteen steps.{p}

Well, {c}{f:|}, you do have the kind of face spirits would love.
But that's not the same as having a strong sixth sense, right?
Ahaha...
.........{p}

Hmm.
But maybe you just missed it.
Maybe something supernatural really did happen...
When I tried it, it was hard to tell, too.
...I'll tell you about it.
Actually, I tried it yesterday.{p}

After school, I snuck into the old school building, even though it's off-limits.
First, I hung the tear-off calendar on the wall by those stairs.
Then I went up from the bottom of the stairs, one step at a time.
And then...{p}

"Eleven, twelve, thirteen... Oh, so there really are fourteen..."
I was so let down.
Standing on the thirteenth step, my shoulders just slumped.
It was so frustrating.
But just in case, I tried putting my foot on the fourteenth step.
And then...{p}

"Eeeeeeeek☆"
The fourteenth step wasn't there!
I could see it with my own eyes, I swear.
But when I stepped onto that fourteenth step, my foot slipped right through the floor, and I fell down.{p}

Under the floor of the stairs... I mean, under the step, it was pitch black.
I kept falling and falling, down through the darkness...
It felt like, am I going to keep falling like this forever?
The pit of my stomach went all shivery.
Then, after a while, the feeling of falling stopped, but...
It wasn't like I hit the ground and stopped.
It was more like I fell slower and slower, and then finally the falling just stopped.
After that, it felt like I was standing all alone in the darkness, in a daze.{p}

And then... there were lots of people standing there.
In the darkness, people and more people were standing all around me, closing me in.
...Do you know what a human pillar is?
Apparently it happened in some country...
It's a ritual where they bury living people inside a building under construction, or in the ground beneath it.
It's supposed to be a prayer to make the building strong.
Well, maybe there were other reasons too.
I don't really know about the rest.
Anyway, the people surrounding me had sad, blank looks on their faces.
I couldn't help thinking they looked like human pillars.{p}

Right then, crying was echoing through the darkness.
Sad, sad voices...{p}

I got kind of scared, and I tried to run away.
But I didn't know where I should run to.
I mean, in front, behind, right, left, above, below, it was all darkness.
But I tried to move forward anyway...
I kicked off the ground and tried to break into a run.
And then... I couldn't go anywhere.
I could feel my feet kicking the ground, but I couldn't move forward at all.
Not only that, I couldn't move my arms or legs either.
And it wasn't like paralysis, where you can't move at all.
I could put strength into my body, and it felt like it would move if I wanted it to, but...
It was no good.
That's when I realized.
This is just like being buried alive in the dirt.
And then...{p}

The people surrounding me vanished, and instead, hand after hand came reaching out of the darkness.
Yes, so many hands, so many.
They had to be the human pillars' hands.
That's what I thought right away.
I thought they were trying to grab me so they could bury me alive.
Of course, I struggled like crazy.
But the hands covered my eyes and nose and mouth.
The more I fought back, the stronger the hands got...
I couldn't breathe.
Tears came out, too.
And then I passed out...{p}

When I came to, I was lying at the bottom of the stairs.
The tear-off calendar had fallen on the floor.
I guess the metal clip holding it up was flimsy.
Since the calendar fell, the thirteen steps' power must have worn off.
That's how I got saved, I think.{p}

Hey, {c}{f:|}.
The story of the thirteen steps was true.
I heard about it later, but when they first built our school, thirteen people died.
And the place where it happened is right around where those thirteen steps are.
It seems there was an accident while they were putting up the scaffolding around there.
And there was a student who offered flowers and grains of rice every day to mourn them.
Apparently that student always left the offerings on the fourteenth step of the thirteen steps.
So there wouldn't be a fourteenth victim.
And for a while, the spirits seemed to have settled down, but...
They say if you count the thirteen steps on Friday the 13th, those spirits wake up.
Because the day those thirteen people died was apparently a Friday.{p}

So in the end, what I saw weren't human pillars after all.
They were still dead people, though, that part doesn't change.
So I bet on each and every one of those steps, there's the spirit of one of the thirteen who died.
...You hear rumors about thirteen steps all over, not just at our school.
Even without thirteen dead people, just having a staircase with thirteen steps is supposed to be bad luck.{p}
But you know...{p}

It doesn't seem like stairs are safe just because they don't have thirteen steps.
Even with fourteen steps, or fifteen, there are all sorts of ways to make it thirteen.
The spirits just have to drag anyone who tries to go past the thirteenth step down into the depths of the earth.
Just like they did to me...{p}

{c}{f:|}.
Next time, why don't you count the stairs in your own house as you go up?
You might discover something new, you know?
Hee hee...
Okay, let's hear the next story.
I wonder what kind of story it'll be this time...?{p}

I see.
Wait, was it because there hasn't been a single Friday the 13th since we started school, so you couldn't try it?
Then I'll tell you.
There's a way to check it even if it isn't Friday the 13th.{p}

Oh, really? You haven't?
Hmm...
Then no matter how much I talk about the old school building, it won't feel real to you, will it?
Forget it, then!
I'll tell a different story.{p}

Let's see...
{c}{f:|}, is there someone you like?
Do you ever want to make someone yours and yours alone?
If you feel that way even a little...
I want you to hear this story.
{c}{f:|}.
Have you ever {f:given|been given} a ring {f:to a girl|by a boy}?
One with a gem, I mean.
Have you ever {f:given a ring with all your heart in it|been given a ring with someone's whole heart in it}?{p}

The story I'm going to tell you now is about a ruby ring.
They say the ruby is the classic red gem, right?
But a ruby isn't crimson{f:, you see|, right}.
It's a color like red with a shadow cast over it{f:, you know|, isn't it}.
When it comes to crimson gems, I think a garnet fits better.
But do you know why the ruby became the classic red gem?
Here's what I think...
The truly valuable rubies are called pigeon's blood{f:, aren't they|, right}.
{f:It means the color of a pigeon's blood, see.|It means the color of a pigeon's blood.}
A ruby's red is a color just like blood.{p}

{c}{f:|}, do you get what I'm saying?
That's right, the color of blood was chosen over crimson.
I think the color of blood has a big effect on people's hearts.
That's why the ruby became the classic red gem, I think.
People often say the ruby's the classic one because it's rare, but I don't think so.
It's because it's the color of blood...
Okay, I'll get to the story about the ring now.{p}

A few years ago, there was a girl at this school named Sayoko Ishikawa.
She was the type who made you want to protect her.
A little quiet, cute, and when she was in trouble, she'd look like she was about to cry...
But the way she held back her tears was just so touching.
She was sweet-natured too, the type of girl who'd never make selfish demands of a guy.{p}

Her boyfriend had given her a ruby ring.
And she treasured it.
Her boyfriend went to a different high school.
His name was Ogura.{p}

They say he worked a part-time job to buy her the ring.
And Ishikawa would secretly wear the ring whenever the teachers weren't looking.
Their relationship was well known in her class, apparently.
But...
The truth is, back then there was someone at school who was in love with Ishikawa.
It was the science teacher, actually...{p}

His name was Mr. Miyama.
Ishikawa wasn't interested in any other man, though.
Mr. Miyama was crazy about Ishikawa, always playing favorites with her and talking to her all the time.
That's kind of a problem, right?
So it seems Mr. Miyama often got warned about it at faculty meetings and stuff.
But he never changed the way he acted, not one bit.
She, for her part, thought he was a bit of a nuisance, but she didn't especially avoid Mr. Miyama or anything.{p}I guess being treated like she was precious didn't feel bad in itself.
Girls can be like that, you know.{p}

Then one day, her boyfriend... Ogura... died of an illness.
She was terribly sad.
She stayed by Ogura's bedside the whole time, holding his hand right up until the moment they parted forever.
They say he looked at the ruby ring on Ishikawa's finger and said this.{p}

No matter what happens from here on, my feelings won't change.
...There was no "from here on."
His death was close at hand.
He must have known that very well himself, and yet.........
A teardrop fell onto the ruby ring on her finger.
"Are you crying?"
He murmured it faintly.
I mustn't cry, she thought.
She didn't want to sink into gloom when they were saying goodbye.
